claim: Alpo4 is a Cys-loop receptor from Alvinella pompejana, an extreme thermophile worm.
source: In this work, we studied orphan receptor Alpo4 from an extreme thermophile worm Alvinella pompejana.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract of the manuscript.

claim: Alpo4 shows remote relation to characterized nACh receptors based on sequence analysis.
source: Sequence analysis points towards its remote relation to characterized nACh receptors.
evidence: Stated in the abstract based on sequence analysis performed.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of Alpo4 was solved with a CHAPS molecule bound to the orthosteric site.
source: We solved the cryo-EM structure of the lophotrochozoan nACh-like receptor in which a CHAPS molecule is tightly bound to the orthosteric site.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract and supported by structural data.

claim: CHAPS binding leads to extension of loop C at the orthosteric site.
source: We show that the binding of CHAPS leads to extending of the loop C at the orthosteric site and a quaternary twist between extracellular and transmembrane domains.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by structural comparison data.

claim: CHAPS binding causes a quaternary twist between extracellular and transmembrane domains.
source: We show that the binding of CHAPS leads to extending of the loop C at the orthosteric site and a quaternary twist between extracellular and transmembrane domains.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by structural comparison data.

claim: Alpo4 has a conserved Trp residue in loop B that is flipped into a self-liganded state in the apo structure.
source: These include a conserved Trp residue in loop B of the ligand binding site which is flipped into an apparent self-liganded state in the apo structure.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by structural data.

claim: The ion pore of Alpo4 is constricted by a ring of methionines near the extracellular entryway.
source: The ion pore of Alpo4 is tightly constricted by a ring of methionines near the extracellular entryway of the channel pore.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by structural data.

claim: Cys-loop receptors are allosterically regulated pentameric ligand-gated ion channels.
source: Cys-loop receptors are allosterically regulated pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs).
evidence: Stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Cys-loop receptors are classified into cation-selective and anion-selective receptors.
source: Functionally pLGICs are classified into cation- and anion-selective receptors.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors and serotonin receptors are examples of cation-selective Cys-loop receptors.
source: The former class is exemplified by nicotinic acetylcholine (nAChRs) and serotonin (5-HT3) receptors (Corringer et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Glycine and GABAA receptors are anion-selective Cys-loop receptors.
source: Anion-selective receptors are comprised of glycine (GlyRs) and GABAA receptors.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Human and mammalian pLGICs have been actively researched due to their role in diseases.
source: Because of their role in synaptic transmission, the inflammatory response and implication in diseases including gastro-intestinal, psychiatric and cognitive disorders, startle disease, epilepsy, and smoking addiction (Treiman, 2001; Albuquerque et al., 2009; Walstab et al., 2010; Ha and Richman, 2015), human and mammalian homologs of pLGICs have been the subject of active research.
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Cryo-EM has led to rapid expansion of structural data on nAChRs.
source: Recent advances in cryo-EM led to a rapid expansion of the structural data on nAChRs.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as a general observation.

claim: Structures of three types of heteropentameric nicotinic receptors (α4β2, α3β4, and Torpedo muscle-nAChR) have been determined.
source: The structures of three types of heteropentameric nicotinic receptors (α4β2, α3β4, and Torpedo muscle-nAChR) and one homopentameric receptor (α7) were determined (Morales-Perez et al., 2016; Walsh et al., 2018; Gharpure et al., 2019; Rahman et al., 2022; Noviello et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Structures of the α7 nicotinic receptor in three major conformational states (resting, activated, and desensitized) have been solved.
source: For the α7 nicotinic receptor, structures of three major conformational states were solved: a resting, an agonist-bound activated, and an agonist-bound desensitized state.
evidence: Stated in the introduction with implicit citation support from previous sentence.

claim: Cryo-EM structures have been determined for 5-HT3 receptors.
source: Cryo-EM structures also have been determined for 5-HT3 receptors (Basak et al., 2018; Polovinkin et al., 2018; Hassaine et al., 2014, glycine receptors Huang et al., 2015; Du et al., 2015), and GABAA receptors (Kim et al., 2020; Masiulis et al., 2019; Zhu et al., 2018; Laverty et al., 2019; Miller and Aricescu, 2014).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Cryo-EM structures have been determined for glycine receptors.
source: Cryo-EM structures also have been determined for 5-HT3 receptors (Basak et al., 2018; Polovinkin et al., 2018; Hassaine et al., 2014, glycine receptors Huang et al., 2015; Du et al., 2015), and GABAA receptors (Kim et al., 2020; Masiulis et al., 2019; Zhu et al., 2018; Laverty et al., 2019; Miller and Aricescu, 2014).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Cryo-EM structures have been determined for GABAA receptors.
source: Cryo-EM structures also have been determined for 5-HT3 receptors (Basak et al., 2018; Polovinkin et al., 2018; Hassaine et al., 2014, glycine receptors Huang et al., 2015; Du et al., 2015), and GABAA receptors (Kim et al., 2020; Masiulis et al., 2019; Zhu et al., 2018; Laverty et al., 2019; Miller and Aricescu, 2014).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Only one structure of a non-vertebrate ion channel, the glutamate-gated chloride channel (GluCl) from C. elegans, has been solved.
source: Currently, only one structure of a non-vertebrate ion channel, the glutamate-gated chloride channel (GluCl), from C. elegans has been solved.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as a factual observation.

claim: GluCl is the drug target for anthelmintics such as ivermectin.
source: GluCl is the drug target for anthelmintics such as ivermectin highlighting the importance of structural characterization of non-vertebrate pLGICs (Althoff et al., 2014; Hibbs and Gouaux, 2011).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Lophotrochozoa includes organisms such as annelids, mollusks, and platyhelminths.
source: Lophotrochozoa comprises one of the largest groups in the animal kingdom and includes organisms such as annelids, mollusks, and platyhelminths (flatworms).
evidence: Stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Genome analysis revealed 52 nAChR genes in mollusks.
source: Intriguingly, genome analysis revealed a massive expansion of nAChR genes in these organisms with 52 and 217 nAChR genes identified in mollusks and annelids, respectively (Jiao et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Genome analysis revealed 217 nAChR genes in annelids.
source: Intriguingly, genome analysis revealed a massive expansion of nAChR genes in these organisms with 52 and 217 nAChR genes identified in mollusks and annelids, respectively (Jiao et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Humans have 17 nAChR genes encoded in their genome.
source: This contrasts with the number of receptors found in organisms having an advanced nervous system, in which only 10–20 nAChRs are encoded in the genomes, for example, 17 in humans (Walsh et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: The expansion in nAChR genes may be a consequence of adaptation to a stationary lifestyle in a dynamic environment.
source: It has been speculated that the expansion in nAChR genes is a consequence of the adaptation to a stationary lifestyle in a dynamic environment (Jiao et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support, presented as speculation.

claim: Seven invertebrate Cys-loop receptors (Alpo1-7) were identified in the proteome of Alvinella pompejana.
source: We have previously biochemically characterized seven invertebrate Cys-loop receptors, Alpo1-7, identified in the proteome of Alvinella pompejana, an annelid worm that inhabits the surroundings of hydrothermal vents and is the most extreme thermophilic invertebrate currently known (Chevaldonné et al., 2000; Holder et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Alvinella pompejana is the most extreme thermophilic invertebrate currently known.
source: We have previously biochemically characterized seven invertebrate Cys-loop receptors, Alpo1-7, identified in the proteome of Alvinella pompejana, an annelid worm that inhabits the surroundings of hydrothermal vents and is the most extreme thermophilic invertebrate currently known (Chevaldonné et al., 2000; Holder et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Alpo1 and Alpo4 are nAChR-like receptors.
source: Among seven Alpo receptors, we identified two nAChR-like receptors (Alpo1 and Alpo4) and one Gly-like receptor (Alpo6), which were expressed and purified in amounts suitable for structural studies (Wijckmans et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Alpo6 is a Gly-like receptor.
source: Among seven Alpo receptors, we identified two nAChR-like receptors (Alpo1 and Alpo4) and one Gly-like receptor (Alpo6), which were expressed and purified in amounts suitable for structural studies (Wijckmans et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Alpo4 has 27–29% sequence identity with α-subunits of nAChRs.
source: Alpo4 has 27–29% sequence identity with α-subunits of nAChRs and 25% with 5-HT3 receptors.
evidence: Stated in the introduction based on sequence analysis.

claim: Alpo4 has 25% sequence identity with 5-HT3 receptors.
source: Alpo4 has 27–29% sequence identity with α-subunits of nAChRs and 25% with 5-HT3 receptors.
evidence: Stated in the introduction based on sequence analysis.

claim: The agonist/neurotransmitter for Alpo4 could not be identified despite exhaustive screening.
source: However, despite exhaustive screening in different expression systems in combination with a compound library, including acetylcholine and serotonin, we could not identify the agonist/neurotransmitter for Alpo4, thereby limiting functional studies (Wijckmans et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: A phylogenetic comparison of Alpo1-4 with nAChRs from various annelids and mollusks was performed.
source: We performed a phylogenetic comparison of Alpo1-4 with nAChRs from annelids: Capitella teleta (CT), Dimorphilus gyrociliatus (DM), Owenia fusiformis (OW), Hirudo verbana (HV), Helobdella robusta (HR), and from mollusca: Crassostrea virginca (MV), Crassostrea gigas (CG), Mizuhopecten yessoensis (MY), Pecten maximus (PM) and Pomacea canaliculata (PC) (Kocot et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in the results section with citation support.

claim: A total of 649 sequences were grouped into 25 families in the phylogenetic analysis.
source: A total of 649 sequences were grouped into 25 families (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Alpo2 and Alpo3 are found in families 32C and 41A with sequence identities of 45% and 65% to the closest homolog, respectively.
source: Alpo2 and 3 are found in the families 32C and 41A (sequence identities of the closest homolog are 45% and 65%, respectively), both of which contain sequences from the genome of each included lophotrochozoan suggesting functional importance and conservation of these protein families within the clade (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure.

claim: The characteristic vicinal disulfide in the tip of loop C is not present in Alpo3-like nAChRs in Polychaeta organisms.
source: Interestingly, in Polychaeta organisms, the characteristic vicinal disulfide in the tip of loop C required for ligand binding is not present in Alpo3-like nAChRs.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on sequence analysis.

claim: Alpo1 and Alpo4 do not cluster in well-populated families, with sequence identities of the closest homolog being 36% and 37%, respectively.
source: On the contrary, Alpo1 and Alpo4 (families 42A and 43A; sequence identities of the closest homolog 36% and 37%) do not clusters in the well-populated families (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Alpo4 was purified in the detergent LMNG.
source: We purified Alpo4 in the detergent LMNG following the protocol established earlier (Wijckmans et al., 2016) and used cryo-EM to solve its structure.
evidence: Stated in the results section with citation support.

claim: The cryo-EM map of Alpo4 was reconstructed to 4.1 Å resolution.
source: The map reconstructed to 4.1 Å resolution confirmed that Alpo4 assembles into a homopentamer and has a conserved architecture of the pLGIC family (Figure 1a, Table 1).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure and table.

claim: Alpo4 assembles into a homopentamer.
source: The map reconstructed to 4.1 Å resolution confirmed that Alpo4 assembles into a homopentamer and has a conserved architecture of the pLGIC family (Figure 1a, Table 1).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure and table.

claim: Alpo4 has a conserved architecture of the pLGIC family.
source: The map reconstructed to 4.1 Å resolution confirmed that Alpo4 assembles into a homopentamer and has a conserved architecture of the pLGIC family (Figure 1a, Table 1).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure and table.

claim: Each Alpo4 subunit is composed of a β-sandwich extracellular domain and a transmembrane domain made of four trans-membrane α-helices M1-M4.
source: Each Alpo4 subunit is composed of a β-sandwich extracellular domain (ECD) and a transmembrane domain (TMD) made of four trans-membrane α-helices M1-M4 (Figure 1b, Figure 1—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: Helices M2 contributed by each subunit are radially arranged around a central ion-conducting pore.
source: Helices M2 contributed by each subunit are radially arranged around a central ion-conducting pore.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data.

claim: The density for the intracellular domain (ICD), residues 308–412, was missing and not modeled.
source: The density for the intracellular domain (ICD), residues 308–412, was missing, and it was consequently not modeled (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure.

claim: An additional density next to the side chain of N167 on ECD was modeled as an N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc).
source: An additional density next to the side chain of N167 on ECD was modeled as an N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc; Figure 1b, Figure 1—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: Glutamine glycosylation at the structurally equivalent position was found in the 5-HT3 receptor, but not in nicotinic receptors.
source: Glutamine glycosylation at the structurally equivalent position was also found in the 5-HT3 receptor, but not in nicotinic receptors (Polovinkin et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated in the results section with citation support.

claim: An additional density was observed in the orthosteric binding site of Alpo4 despite no ligand being added.
source: Although no ligand was added, an additional density was observed in the orthosteric binding site located at the interface between the ECDs (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 4a).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: The additional density in the orthosteric binding site was consistent with a CHAPS molecule.
source: Despite the limited resolution, this density was well-resolved and consistent with a CHAPS molecule, a steroid-derived detergent.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data.

claim: CHAPS was present in the purified Alpo4 at a concentration of 0.007% (110 μM).
source: CHAPS was present in the purified Alpo4 at a concentration of 0.007% (110 μM) because of its thermostabilizing effect on Alpo4 (Wijckmans et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the results section with citation support.

claim: The CHAPS concentration of 110 μM is 70-fold lower than the critical micellar concentration (CMC) of the detergent.
source: At 110 μM, the CHAPS concentration is 70-fold lower than the critical micellar concentration (CMC) of the detergent, suggesting a specific interaction with Alpo4 beyond modulating properties of the detergent belt and, therefore, is consistent with CHAPS binding to the orthosteric site (Petroff et al., 2022).
evidence: Stated in the results section with citation support and inference.

claim: The ECD comprises an amino-terminal α-helix followed by 10 β-strands folded into a β-sandwich.
source: The ECD comprises an amino-terminal α-helix followed by 10 β-strands folded into a β-sandwich (Figure 1b, Figure 1—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: CHAPS is bound at the ligand-binding pocket located at the interface of the principal (loops A-C) and the complementary subunit (loops D-F).
source: CHAPS is bound at the ligand-binding pocket located at the interface of the principal (loops A-C) and the complementary subunit (loops D-F; Figure 2a and d).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: The CHAPS-Alpo4 interactions can be divided into two regions: the hydrophilic moiety and the sterol-binding moiety.
source: The CHAPS-Alpo4 interactions can be divided into two regions: the hydrophilic moiety and the sterol-binding moiety (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure.

claim: The quaternary ammonium group of CHAPS establishes a cation-π interaction with W159.
source: Here, the quaternary ammonium group of the CHAPS molecule establishes a cation-π interaction with W159 (Figure 2a and d).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: The interaction with the hydrophilic moiety is stabilized by a salt bridge between the sulfonate group of CHAPS and Alpo4-specific Arg171.
source: The interaction with the hydrophilic moiety is further stabilized by a salt bridge between the sulfonate group of CHAPS and Alpo4-specific Arg171 (Figure 2a).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure.

claim: The sterol ring moiety of CHAPS fits into a hydrophobic crevice with high shape-complementarity.
source: The sterol ring moiety of CHAPS is composed of three cyclohexane and one cyclopentane ring and it fits into a hydrophobic crevice with a high shape-complementarity.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data.

claim: The sterol ring interacts with residues F103, N104, F137, V155, and W197 on the principal side and residues V48, K49, and D181 on the complementary side via Van der Waals contacts.
source: The sterol ring interacts with residues F103 (loop A), N104, F137, V155, and W197 on the principal side and residues V48, K49, and D181 on the complementary side exclusively via Van der Waals contacts (Figure 2a, Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: The hydrophobic crevice for CHAPS binding is specific to Alpo4 and is lined by poorly conserved residues.
source: This hydrophobic crevice is specific to Alpo4 and it is lined by poorly conserved residues.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural comparison.

claim: The highest resolution reconstruction of Alpo4 in the apo state was 3.4 Å.
source: The highest resolution reconstruction of 3.4 Å was obtained from the protein sample that was depleted of CHAPS using size-exclusion chromatography (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure.

claim: In the apo state, the density corresponding to the tip of the C- and F- loops was less well resolved, indicating increased flexibility.
source: Despite the higher overall resolution of the reconstruction, the density corresponding to the tip of the C- and the F- loops was less well resolved which indicates their increased flexibility in the absence of a ligand.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data and inference.

claim: At low sigma levels, residual densities were observed in the ligand-binding and sterol-binding pockets of the apo state, suggesting residual CHAPS was bound at low occupancy.
source: At low sigma levels, residual densities were observed in the ligand-binding and the sterol-binding pockets suggesting that residual CHAPS was bound at low occupancy.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data and inference.

claim: The structure of Alpo4 prepared in LMNG without CHAPS was reconstructed to 4.1 Å and is essentially identical to the apo state with RMSD of 0.9 Å.
source: Similar results were obtained from the sample prepared in LMNG without CHAPS, reconstructed to 4.1 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 6). This structure is essentially identical to the apo state with (RMSD of 0.9 Å) (Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: In the apo state, W159 (loop B) flips and forms a cation-π interaction with H131.
source: The conformation of the aromatic residues constituting the ligand-binding pocket differed from the CHAPS-bound state. Specifically, W159 (loop B) flips and forms a cation-π interaction with H131, while being pinched by W65 (loop D) (Figure 2f).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure.

claim: The conformation of W159 in the apo state represents a 'self-liganded' state.
source: In this conformation, W159 can no longer form a cation-π interaction with an external ligand, therefore, it is tempting to speculate that this conformation represents a 'self-liganded' state.
evidence: Stated in the results section as speculation based on structural data.

claim: Structures of Alpo4 with added acetylcholine or serotonin were solved to resolutions of 3.9 Å and 6.2 Å, respectively.
source: To determine the agonistic activity of hit compounds identified from virtual screening, all compounds were applied to oocytes injected with Alpo4 RNA. Mean currents elicited by a 10 s application were compared to uninjected cells, and compared to an application of a control solvent (ND96, EtOH, or DMSO). No compounds were found to elicit significantly different currents between Alpo4 or uninjected cells, with the exception of diosgenin.
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: No density in the ligand-binding site was observed in the reconstructions with acetylcholine.
source: Their overall conformation was identical to that of the apo state with an overall RMSD of 0.87 and 0.88 Å, respectively. No density in the ligand-binding site was observed in the reconstructions.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data.

claim: The overall quaternary structure of Alpo4 with serotonin was identical to that of the apo state.
source: Although 6.2 Å resolution is too low to interpret the density of serotonin, the overall quaternary structure was identical to that of the apo state.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data.

claim: The absence of a quaternary twist in the serotonin-treated structure suggests that serotonin was not bound.
source: The absence of a quaternary twist expected for a desensitized conformation suggests that serotonin was not bound.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data and inference.

claim: Neither acetylcholine nor serotonin binds Alpo4 based on cryo-EM reconstructions.
source: The cryo-EM reconstructions of Alpo4 obtained in the presence of acetylcholine and serotonin suggest that neither of the neurotransmitters binds Alpo4.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data.

claim: Electrophysiological experiments indicated no agonist response to acetylcholine or serotonin.
source: This agrees with our electrophysiological experiments in various expression systems (Xenopus oocytes, HEK cells, lipid vesicles) indicating no agonist response to acetylcholine or serotonin (data not shown).
evidence: Stated in the results section based on experimental data.

claim: Upon binding of CHAPS, the ECD rotates 9° clockwise relative to the TMD when viewed from the extracellular side.
source: Upon binding of CHAPS, the ECD rotates 9° clockwise relative to the TMD (when viewed from the extracellular side; Figure 3a and b).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: The tip of loop C shifts by about 3 Å and extends upon CHAPS binding.
source: First, the tip of the loop C (residues 197–205) shifts by about 3 Å and extends (Figure 3a and d) even though its density in the apo state is somewhat ambiguous (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: Loop F shifts by 3–5 Å toward the sterol group of CHAPS on the complementary subunit.
source: On the complimentary subunit, loop F (residues 171–184) shifts by 3–5 Å toward the sterol group of CHAPS.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data.

claim: The ECD protomers rotate by ~3 degrees around the domain center upon CHAPS binding.
source: The ECD protomers show concerted movements as rigid bodies. They rotate by ~3 degrees around the domain center such that the apical regions of ECD move in the direction of neighboring ECD subunit in a clockwise fashion, whereases TMD-facing ends move counterclockwise (Figure 3a, Video 1).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure and video.

claim: The quaternary rearrangements preserve the hydrophobic CHAPS-binding groove even though its width changes.
source: The quaternary rearrangements preserve the hydrophobic CHAPS-binding groove (Figure 3f and g) even though its width changes.
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to figures.

claim: A quaternary twist is associated with gating transitions in characterized pLGICs.
source: A quaternary twist is associated with gating transitions in characterized pLGICs (Noviello et al., 2021; Basak et al., 2018; Polovinkin et al., 2018; Zarkadas et al., 2022; Petroff et al., 2022; Sauguet et al., 2014; Kumar et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated in the results section with citation support.

claim: Quaternary changes in Alpo4 induced by CHAPS binding and those associated with activation of α7 nACh and 5-HT3 receptors induce rotation of ECD relative to TMD in the same direction.
source: Quaternary changes in Alpo4 induced upon CHAPS binding and those associated with the activation of related α7 nACh and 5-HT3 receptors induced rotation of ECD relative to TMD in the same direction, however, the shifts of principal relative to complementary subunits were different (Video 2).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a video.

claim: In Alpo4, the complementary subunit slides upward upon CHAPS binding.
source: In Alpo4, the complementary subunit slides upward whereas in the two other channels, it consistently shifts towards the principal subunit and tilts relative to the TMD.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural comparison.

claim: The tilt in Alpo4 is less pronounced than in α7 nACh and 5-HT3 receptors, which is probably why it does not lead to pore dilation.
source: The tilt is less pronounced in Alpo4 which is probably why it does not lead to the pore dilation.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural comparison and inference.

claim: All four TM helices in the TMD are well resolved allowing for unambiguous assignment of the helix register.
source: In the TMD, all four TM helices are well resolved allowing for unambiguous assignment of the helix register.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data.

claim: The ion pore has a circa 15 Å long hydrophobic patch in the outer leaflet of the membrane formed by three helical turns (residues 9'L, 13'L, and 16'M).
source: The ion pore is located along the fivefold rotational symmetry axis and is formed exclusively by the M2 helices. It has a circa 15 Å long hydrophobic patch in the outer leaflet of the membrane formed by three helical turns (residues 9'L, 13'L, and 16'M; Figure 4a).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure.

claim: The hydrophobic region of the pore is flanked by negatively charged aspartate residues (20'D) on the extracellular side.
source: On the extracellular side, the hydrophobic region is flanked by negatively charged aspartate residues, 20'D, whereas on the intracellular side glycines G'6 create a cavity within the pore (Figure 4b) followed by rings of threonines (2'T) and conserved glutamates (–1'E) which usually play a role of the selectivity filter in cation-selective pLGICs (Yonekura et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the results section with reference to a figure and citation.

claim: The charge distribution along the pore is consistent with Alpo4 being selective for cations.
source: Thus, the charge distribution along the pore is consistent with Alpo4 being selective for cations.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data and inference.

claim: Alpo4 has bulky M265 residues at the 16' position forming the narrowest and most hydrophobic constriction (diameter of 2.1 Å).
source: A highly unusual feature in Alpo4 is the presence of bulky M265 residues at the 16' position. It forms the narrowest and most hydrophobic constriction (diameter of 2.1 Å) that likely functions as a gate.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on structural data.

claim: Constriction at the 16' position is absent in other structurally characterized nAChRs but was observed in the bacterial Cys-loop receptor homolog ELIC.
source: Constriction at this position is absent in other structurally characterized nAChRs but was observed in the bacterial Cys-loop receptor homolog ELIC in which the pore is constricted by a Phe residue at the extracellular surface (Ulens et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated in the results section with citation support.

claim: The M16'L mutation of Alpo4 was unresponsive to acetylcholine or serotonin.
source: Therefore, we explored an M16'L mutation, which unfortunately was also unresponsive to acetylcholine or serotonin (data not shown).
evidence: Stated in the results section based on experimental data.

claim: The double mutant M16'L/L9'T of Alpo4 was unresponsive to acetylcholine or serotonin.
source: In our experiments, the double mutant M16'L/L9'T was still unresponsive to acetylcholine or serotonin.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on experimental data.

claim: Chimeras in which the ECD and TMD of Alpo4 were swapped with the α7 nAChR remained unresponsive.
source: Additionally, we constructed chimeras in which the ECD and TMD were swapped with the α7 nAChR, similar to the α7/5-HT3 chimera (Eiselé et al., 1993), but these constructs also remained unresponsive.
evidence: Stated in the results section with citation support and experimental data.

claim: No channel activity was detected in the presence of oxidizing (H2O2) or reducing agents (DTT).
source: However, we could not detect any channel activity in the presence of oxidizing (H2O2) or reducing agents (DTT) (data not shown).
evidence: Stated in the results section based on experimental data.

claim: Virtual screening was performed using 37,000 compounds on three conformations of the Alpo4 receptor.
source: To deorphanize Alpo4, we performed virtual screening using 37,000 compounds on three conformations of the Alpo4 receptor (see Methods for details).
evidence: Stated in the results section based on computational methods.

claim: Several top compounds from virtual screening contain sterol-like moieties.
source: Several of the top compounds contain sterol-like moieties including the top hit from virtual screening, ZINC36126889, which has an average binding energy of –12.1 kcal/mol (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Stated in the results section based on computational screening.

claim: ZINC36126889 is a natural product synthesized by various species of Solanum plants and contains the sapogenin backbone structure.
source: This is a natural product synthesized by various species of Solanum plants and contains the sapogenin backbone structure.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on compound information.

claim: Diosgenin is a bioactive steroid sapogenin synthesized by a range of plant species.
source: These compounds are structurally similar to diosgenin – a bioactive steroid sapogenin that is synthesized by a range of plant species (Jesus et al., 2016) and has been shown to bind in the orthosteric pocket of the chemo-tactile receptor from the striped pyjama squid (Sepioloidea lineolata) (van Giesen et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated in the results section with citation support.

claim: No compounds tested were found to elicit significantly different currents between Alpo4 or uninjected cells, with the exception of diosgenin.
source: To determine the agonistic activity of hit compounds identified from virtual screening, all compounds were applied to oocytes injected with Alpo4 RNA. Mean currents elicited by a 10 s application were compared to uninjected cells, and compared to an application of a control solvent (ND96, EtOH, or DMSO). No compounds were found to elicit significantly different currents between Alpo4 or uninjected cells, with the exception of diosgenin.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on electrophysiological data.

claim: The highest concentration (100 µM) of diosgenin elicited a significantly greater current in uninjected cells compared to Alpo4, suggesting it may be disrupting the cell membrane.
source: The highest concentration (100 µM) of diosgenin was found to elicit a significantly greater current in uninjected cells compared to Alpo4, which suggests it may be disrupting the cell membrane.
evidence: Stated in the results section based on electrophysiological data and inference.

claim: Alpo4 lacks signature amino acids of an α-like nAChR subunit.
source: Multiple sequence alignment shows the presence of key aromatic ligand-binding residues and the absence of the characteristic vicinal disulfide in the tip of loop C indicating that Alpo4 lacks signature amino acids of an α-like nAChR subunit (Albuquerque et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with citation support.

claim: Alpo4 might be gated by a ligand different from acetylcholine and serotonin.
source: Alpo4 might be gated by a ligand different from acetylcholine and serotonin consistent with the expansion of nACh genes in lophotrochozoan.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section as speculation based on data.

claim: Marine organisms such as octopus and squid have nACh-like chemotactile receptors that do not respond to acetylcholine but are gated by poorly soluble terpenes and chloroquine.
source: It has recently been discovered that other marine organisms such as octopus and squid have nACh-like chemotactile receptors that do not respond to acetylcholine but are gated by poorly soluble terpenes and chloroquine (van Giesen et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with citation support.

claim: The 16'M pore constriction is not a thermophile-specific residue, as it is also present in sequences of nAChRs-like proteins from mesophile organisms.
source: It is worth noting, that 16'M is not a thermophile-specific residue, as it is also present in the sequences of nAChRs-like proteins from mesophile organisms such as Pecten maximus and Gigantopelta aegis.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section based on sequence analysis.

claim: Alpo5 and Alpo6 were identified as glycine receptors with glycine as the agonist.
source: This, however, contradicts the electrophysiological experiments that allowed us to identify glycine as the agonist for Alpo5 and Alpo6, which displayed high sequence similarity to glycine receptors (45–50%) (Wijckmans et al., 2016), whereas Alpo7 was identified as a pH-gated ion channel (Juneja et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with citation support.

claim: Alpo7 was identified as a pH-gated ion channel.
source: This, however, contradicts the electrophysiological experiments that allowed us to identify glycine as the agonist for Alpo5 and Alpo6, which displayed high sequence similarity to glycine receptors (45–50%) (Wijckmans et al., 2016), whereas Alpo7 was identified as a pH-gated ion channel (Juneja et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with citation support.

claim: His131 on loop E could potentially coordinate a metal ion or require (de)protonation for the channel to become responsive to an agonist.
source: Another unusual feature of the apo structure of Alpo4 is the presence of His131 on loop E, which forms a cation-π interaction with the highly conserved loop B aromatic W159 in the orthosteric binding site. The histidine could potentially coordinate a metal ion or require (de)protonation for the channel to become responsive to an agonist.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section as speculation based on structural data.

claim: CHAPS is not expected to be a native ligand in Alvinella pompejana.
source: Although CHAPS is not expected to be a native ligand in Alvinella pompejana, our structures reveal it interacts with the ECD and induces a quaternary twist movement.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section based on inference.

claim: Pharmaceutical α7 nAChR agonists are composed of three representative groups: a cationic center, a hydrogen bond acceptor, and a hydrophobic element.
source: Pharmaceutical α7 nAChR agonists are composed of three representative groups: a cationic center, a hydrogen bond acceptor, and a hydrophobic element (Mazurov et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with citation support.

claim: CHAPS binding creates a precedent for the binding of a channel modulator that interacts with two regions of the ECD.
source: Here, the example of CHAPS binding creates an unusual precedent for the binding of a channel modulator that interacts with two regions of the ECD, one in the conserved ligand-binding pocket and another with the poorly conserved crevice outside the orthosteric site (Figures 1, 3f and g, Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Stated in the discussion section based on structural data.

claim: A nanobody bound to ELIC in a site covering the sterol-binding groove was identified, but its interactions with ELIC did not overlap significantly with the interior of the sterol-binding groove.
source: When binding sites of larger known binders, including VHH (Brams et al., 2020; Hénault et al., 2019) and α-bungarotoxin (Noviello et al., 2021; Rahman et al., 2020) were examined (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a) a nanobody bound to ELIC in the site covering the sterol-binding groove was identified, however, its interactions with ELIC did not overlap significantly with the interior of the sterol-binding groove.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with citation support.

claim: The sterol-binding groove is a novel target location for binders.
source: This suggests that the latter is a novel target location for binders.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section based on inference from structural comparison.

claim: The changes in the groove shape are not specific to Alpo4 but are also observed in the nicotinic α7 receptor.
source: The changes in the groove shape are not specific to Alpo4 but are also observed, for example, in the nicotinic α7 receptor (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b) suggesting that the groove can be targeted for allosteric modulation of the channel.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with reference to a figure.

claim: The binding of CHAPS hints at a possible strategy for designing specific Cys-loop channel modulators wherein the orthosteric binder is complemented by a chemical group binding at the interface between the subunits.
source: This finding hints at a possible strategy for designing specific Cys-loop channel modulators wherein the orthosteric binder is complemented by a chemical group binding at the interface between the subunits.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section as speculation based on structural findings.

claim: The structures of chemotactile receptors CRT1 from octopus and CRB1 from squid were reported while this manuscript was under revision.
source: While this manuscript was under revision, the structures of chemotactile receptors (CRs) CRT1 from octopus and CRB1 from squid, which do not respond to acetylcholine but instead to terpenes and bitter tastants like denatonium, were reported (Kang et al., 2023; Allard et al., 2023).
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with citation support.

claim: CRT1 was found to bind and be activated by steroid-like diosgenin moiety and similar molecules that structurally resemble CHAPS.
source: Curiously, CRT1 was found to bind and be activated by steroid-like diosgenin moiety and similar molecules that structurally resemble CHAPS.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section with implicit citation support.

claim: The mode of binding of diosgenin to CRT1 was different from that of CHAPS to Alpo4, and the sterol-binding groove was not involved in the interactions.
source: Nonetheless, their mode of binding to CRT1 was different from that of CHAPS to Alpo4, and the sterol-binding groove was not involved in the interactions.
evidence: Stated in the discussion section based on comparison with cited structures.
